The response also replaces the generic '3-star premium branding package' and explains why. Some names stay vaguer. 'Booth [large]/[small]' says nothing about what the booth includes. expectations.text: Names each perk with a container word that signals its format instead of describing it generically
expectations.evidence: Most benefit rows use a word that names the format: 'Conference passes', 'Booth' (with '3×3 m'), 'Speaking slot' (with '20 min'), 'Social media mentions', 'Logo on website and signage'. The exclusives are named for the physical item: 'Lanyard', 'Coffee cart', 'After-party'. Some rows are still generic or hedged: 'Attendee list or lead scanning' leaves the format open, 'Logo in slides, programme, post-event email' is a bundle, and the after-party says only 'Branding at the venue'.
